channel.notes: OSM: 0 fairway/channel feature(s), 0 lock feature(s), 0 breakwater feature(s) in the rectangle. Channel depth and width are NOT in this dataset.

cranes.note: OSM man_made=crane objects (gantry, portal and mobile cranes alike); OSM crane coverage is incomplete, so this is a lower bound, not a terminal inventory.

sources.name: Rodrigue & Notteboom, Port Economics, Management and Policy: stacking density of container yard equipment (straddle carrier 500-700 TEU/ha, RTG 500-1000 TEU/ha); m2_per_teu = 10000 / 625 TEU/ha = 16 m2 gross yard area per TEU slot (SOURCED range 10-20 m2, value chosen inside it: TEMPORARY point value)

Container berth length = ship length overall + ~10% clearance (30,000 TEU study: 453 m ship occupies 498 m of quay, MDPI J. Mar. Sci. Eng. 7(5) 131, 2019); the 300 m mean_loa_m for container ships is a TEMPORARY assumption between feeder (~200 m) and ULCV (~400 m) tonnage, not a sourced fleet mean
Whole-terminal gross area per TEU slot (m2_per_teu_terminal_gross = 25): TEMPORARY, assumes stacking blocks are ~65% of a terminal polygon; no source found
Anchorage swing radius 400 m (= 300 m LOA + ~3 x 30 m depth, common planning rule) and hex packing 0.9069: TEMPORARY

provenance.basis: MODELLED estimates from SOURCED OSM geometry
